full_judgment: 5. Mr. Shahidul Islam the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the appellants and Mr. A.K.M. Shamsul Karim the learned Assistant Attorney General appeared for the State. At the outset the learned Advocate for the appellants Mr. Shahidul Islam has taken us through the impugned judgment F.I.R. charge charge sheet the evidence on record and other materials including the sketch map and 342 statements of the accused persons. Then he has seriously assailed the judgment and order of conviction of sentence passed by the learned Sessions Judge. His first submission is that the prosecution has totally failed to prove its case beyond all reasonable doubt vis-a-vis the place time and the manner of occurrence as alleged. His second submission is that it is in fact a case of no evidence as such the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence is wholly bad and illegal and the same should be set aside. His next contention is that admittedly there is no eye-witness to the effect that the accused appellants murdered the victim. In the instant case the conviction of the accused has been solely based on the circumstantial evidence particularly, the circumstance relating to the victim being last seen in the company of the appellants and this circumstance is alleged to have been proved by P.W.6 Md. Mokbul Hossain. But on scrutiny of the evidence and the facts and circumstances of the case it would be found that P. W. 6 is not an eye-witness and there are material discrepancies in his deposition. As such the conviction of the accused persons on the basis of such unreliable circumstantial evidence cannot be sustained in law and hence the same should be set aside. His further submission is that there has been serious embellishment of the prosecution story as given by P.W.1 the informant. In his First Information Report and as a result there has been occasion for reasonable doubt about the involvement of the appellants in the commission of the murder of the victim. His next contention is that the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence has been passed mainly on surmises and conjectures and not on legal and reliable evidence. Lastly it is submitted by the learned Advocate for the appellants that non-production of some F.I.R. named material witnesses should have given rise to an adverse presumption against the prosecution case. With the above submissions the learned Advocate for the appellants humbly prays that the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence should be set aside and the appellants be acquitted of the charges levelled against them and they be set at liberty.
